To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

grain micronutrient concentration in Chinese maize grains varied geospatially and was affected by grain yield, N, P, and soil pH, and that grain yield, N rate, and P rate were the key factors that affect grain nutrient status.

the concentrations of grain Zn, Fe, Cu and Mn varied substantially at a national scale in China, and grain Zn, Mn, and Cu concentrations correlated positively with the available concentrations of Zn, Cu, and Mn in soil, and negatively with maize yield.
maize grains in China are generally deficient in Zn and Fe, and that the concentrations of these two micronutrients vary geospatially and are negatively related to maize yield.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the overall status and spatial variation of maize grain micronutrients and identifies the major drivers of geospatial variation in grain micronutrients in China, which is helpful to develop effective measures to improve maize nutritional quality.

the overall status and spatial variation of micronutrient concentrations and the key drivers of maize grain micronutrient accumulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

grain Fe and Mn concentrations are not affected by soil properties, but are affected by grain yield, N rate and soil organic matter; while grain Zn and Cu are mainly determined by soil properties, such as available Zn, Mn, Cu, soil pH, and organic matter, as well as by grain yield, and N and P rate.
grain micronutrient concentration in maize is mainly affected by the grain yield, soil N and P availability, soil pH and soil organic matter.

the concentrations of micronutrient in maize grain in China were generally low, and the grain micronutrient contents varied substantially in the four test regions, with higher levels in southwest China, and the concentrations of Zn and Fe in grain were far below the biofortification targets, while the concentrations of Mn and Cu were higher.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

grain micronutrient levels were significantly lower than the recommended values and varied geospatially in China, and grain Zn, Fe, Cu concentrations and grain yield were negatively correlated in most test areas, suggesting a need for further improvement in grain micronutrients in China.

the current grain quality of maize in China is still far below the biofortification targets, and the grain micronutrient levels are mainly determined by soil properties and crop management practices, especially the application of N and P fertilizer.
maize production should be optimized to achieve a balanced output between energy and nutrients, and the micronutrient concentrations should be improved in maize grain for better human health.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the concentrations of grain micronutrients vary substantially across China, and the concentrations of grain Zn and Fe are still far below the biofortification targets.
maize grain micronutrient contents are geographically variable, and grain Zn and Fe are deficient in most maize production regions of the country.
the concentrations of grain Fe, Zn, Mn and P are not adequate in the major maize production areas, and that the grain Zn concentration is lower than the biofortification targets.
